Advocate ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Mr. Ramesh Sinha, Chief Justice Order on Board 12-07-2024 1.

This is the first bail application filed under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of regular bail to the applicant who has been arrested on 10-01-2024 in connection with Crime No. 13 of 2024 registered at Police Station - Sakri, District Bilaspur ( C.G.) for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(3), 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 5(L)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

sentences.text: Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that the mother of the prosecutrix lodged a report that on 8-1-2024 at about 4.30 pm her minor daughter aged about 14 years came from school and at that time complainant went to collect the clothes which were dried outside of the house.
When she came inside the house, the prosecutrix changed school uniform and wore other clothes and went outside by saying that she will Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:25089 come very soon.
The complainant followed her but after some time complainant did not see her daughter then complainant came back to her house and informed her husband.
They started searching their minor daughter but she was not found.

Thereafter they went to police station and lodged report on the basis of which Police Station Sakri District Bilaspur registered FIR bearing Crime No 13 dof 2024 for the offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC and initiated investigation.
During investigation prosecutrix was recovered from the possession of the present applicant on 9-1-2024
On the basis of the memorandum statement of the prosecutrix, the Police added Sections 366 and 376 of IPC and Section 4 and 6 of POCSO Act, 2012and arrested the present applicant/accused.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He further submit that the father and mother of the prosecutrix have not supported the actual date of birth of the prosecutrix and they have not supported the case of the prosecution.

Further he is in jail since 10-1-2024 and a young boy, the long detention of the applicant will adversely affect his future and family and conclusion of trial may take some time,
hence he prays for grant of bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the State/non- applicant opposes the bail application of the applicant and submits that though the parents of the prosecutrix have not supported the case of the prosecution, but the prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C., has supported the case of prosecution and she was below the age of 18 years at the time of incident.
Hence the bail application of the applicant is liable to be dismissed.
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:25089 5.
I have heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the case diary.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions of learned counsel for the parties, and also considering the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C and the manner in which the offence has been committed by the applicant, this court is of the opinion that it is not a fit case to enlarge the applicant on bail.

7. Accordingly, the bail application of the applicant Dhruw Kumar Suryavanshi filed under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C., involved in Crime No. 13 of 2024 registered at Police Station Sakri, District Bilaspur ( C.G.) for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(3), 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 5(L)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.
